Hi Jordan / Priya,

Great talking with you today — thanks for walking through the prototype and the long-document use case. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can stay aligned: 

What we heard from ACME: 
- Primary goal: reliably summarize and extract decisions from long RFPs and program reports (20k–50k tokens).
- Key constraints: strict PII handling, consistent summarization fidelity, and predictable latency for near-real-time review workflows.
- Success metric: summaries that preserve all decision-critical bullets (precision > 0.9 on our eval set) and no missing action items.

Our recommendations (initial):
1) Model candidates: a long-context variant with >64k context window for full-document runs (we recommend trying Redwood-Long-32k and Redwood-Long-65k variants as first pass); if latency is a blocker, test Redwood-Lite-8k with our prefix-KV streaming config for chunked summarization.
2) Eval plan: we’ll run long-context evals on your sample corpus measuring truncation behavior, hallucination rate, and summarization fidelity (ROUGE + an extractive decision recall test).
3) Prompt set: attached is a starter prompt set (prompt_set_acme_v1.jsonl) tailored to RFPs and decision extraction. Please review and flag any domain-specific wording you want included.
4) Next steps:
   - You: share 5 representative docs (redacted as needed) and a list of must-capture fields.
   - Us: run a 1-week eval across the 2 model variants + our streaming chunking baseline, provide benchmark report (latency, token cost, fidelity).
   - Optional: we can stand up a short trial environment (Dedicated trial or hosted sandbox) to let your team run live experiments.

Links & artifacts:
- Redwood long-context benchmark (public): https://app.redwood.ai/benchmarks/long-context-2026
- Attached: prompt_set_acme_v1.jsonl (starter prompts)

Questions for you:
- Do you have an internal SLA on latency per doc?
- Any internal reviewers (security/compliance) we should loop in for the sample transfer?

Thanks — I’ll loop in Rishi (SE) and Naomi (Prod) to propose the eval configuration once we have samples.

Best,

Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — looping in my plan below. High-level answers first:
- Feasibility: Yes — Redwood-Long-32k should meet the 8s median for typical 20k-token docs with our optimized KV streaming and continuous batching (on dedicated gpus, typical p95 ~ 12s). For 50k tokens we recommend Redwood-Long-65k to avoid cross-chunk merging overhead; expected median ~18–24s depending on GPU class and I/O. Exact numbers depend on your chosen instance class; I’ll give two SKU profiles in the attached PDF.

Proposed eval configuration (summary):
- Models to test: Redwood-Long-32k, Redwood-Long-65k, Redwood-Lite-8k (chunked + streaming).
- Runtime settings: enable prefix KV caching, continuous batching w/ max batch 8, streaming chunk size 8k tokens with overlap 256 tokens (to reduce boundary loss).
- Diagnostics:
  * Truncation diagnostic: token-offset maps per doc, highlight first/last dropped tokens per section, and a binary flag per section if >5% of tokens truncated.
  * Fidelity heatmap: per-section recall for must-capture fields (visual + CSV output).
  * Hallucination checks: NER agreement and citation checks against the source doc.
- Outputs: benchmark HTML (redwood-benchmark-longcontext-2026.html), PDF executive summary (long_context_eval_recs.pdf), and the run prompt_set (attached prompt_set_acme_v1.jsonl).

Next steps & timeline:
1) ACME: drop 5 representative redacted docs to our SFTP by Mon 03/02 EOD (we'll provide login).
2) Redwood: run baseline 48-hour eval across the 3 variants; deliver artifacts (HTML + PDF) and a short walkthrough call.
3) If results show model regressions on a required metric, we’ll propose either a model variant swap or prompt/chain-of-thought adjustments and re-run targeted tests.

Attachments: prompt_set_acme_v1.jsonl (13 KB), long_context_eval_recs.pdf (44 KB), redwood-benchmark-longcontext-2026.html (160 KB)

Notes for Marissa / Naomi: I included two SKU latency profiles in the PDF and a recommended default: g4dn-large equivalent for L32k testing, p4d-small equivalent for L65k if you want lower p95. Naomi — can you confirm the proposed fidelity metric (ROUGE + decision recall) is fine or suggest thresholds?
